title: Every admitted write job reaches its writer, once
body: The software shall carry each write job a submitter admits (a pointer to the caller's job) from the submitting thread to its environment's one writer thread, each job delivered exactly once and none lost, whatever the number of threads submitting at once.
rationale: Every durable write of the box (the drive's files, the estate's records, the rms's items and security log) is a job of kyr_core's queue; a lost job leaves its submitter waiting for ever, a duplicated one runs a write twice.
criteria: Jobs handed over by many threads to one arrive once each, none lost, none duplicated, under load and under the thread sanitizer.

title: Many submitters at once, none waiting on another
body: Any number of request threads shall hand jobs over at the same time without a lock and without waiting on one another; a hand-off on a full ring shall refuse at once, so that the submitter retries within its admission budget (250 ms, every 0.2 ms) and then refuses the write.
rationale: The box's request threads all write; a hand-off that waited on another submitter would serialise them, one that blocked on a full ring would hold a request thread beyond its budget.
criteria: A hand-off on a full ring returns a refusal at once; concurrent hand-offs from many threads all complete; no lock is on the hand-off's path.

title: A bounded ring per environment, allocated once
body: Each environment's ring shall hold a number of jobs fixed when the queue starts (1024), every slot usable, its memory taken once at the start; nothing shall be allocated on the request path.
rationale: kyr_core's queue is static by doctrine: a fixed pool of completion slots sized from the ring's capacity, nothing allocated after the start.
criteria: A ring of 1024 takes 1024 jobs before it refuses one; the hand-off and the take allocate nothing.

title: The writer takes batches without waiting
body: The environment's writer shall take up to 32 jobs at a time, each take answering at once whether there was one, and shall learn from its own thread, before it sleeps on its condition, whether a job is waiting.
rationale: The writer commits one durable parent transaction per batch; a take that blocked would stop every write of its environment.
criteria: Taking from an empty ring answers 'none' at once; the emptiness check from the writer's thread is consistent with its next take.

title: A preempted submitter delays, never loses
body: The software may delay the delivery of the jobs behind a submitter preempted inside its own hand-off, but shall never lose, duplicate or tear a job because of it; delivery shall resume when that submitter runs on.
rationale: The platform accepts a ring that is not formally lock-free: its submitters hold no lock and make no blocking call inside the hand-off and wake the writer after it, so the window is a few instructions of a running thread.
criteria: An analysis of the claim-to-publish window; the threaded suites deliver every job once under contention.

title: The writer's role passes to the stopping thread
body: At the queue's stop the writer thread is joined and the stopping thread drains what is left, so that no submitter waits for ever: the ring shall accept its consumer changing from one thread to another across a thread join.
rationale: Shutdown answers every admitted job (INTERNAL) instead of abandoning it.
criteria: A drain by another thread after the consumer's join takes every job left, once.

title: Delivered as the platform pins its libraries
body: The software shall be delivered as the Debian packages libmpscring and libmpscring-dev, tier 1 of the platform (no platform dependency of its own), built reproducibly and pinned by the platform by version and SHA-256 in deps.txt.
rationale: kyr_core, kyr_drive, kyr_estate, kyr_rms, the box's servers and the platform's train resolve it from deps.txt.
criteria: The packages install and a program built against them alone runs; two builds give the same bytes; the pins resolve.

title: Qualified under the platform's build profiles
body: Each release the platform pins shall be built and tested under the platform's kyr-build profiles (release, sanitizers, thread sanitizer, coverage), its pipeline green at the release commit.
rationale: The ring carries the box's writes between threads; the platform annotates the hand-off for its own thread-sanitizer builds because the library it links is not instrumented, and takes no release whose concurrent paths have not run under the thread sanitizer.
criteria: The release pipeline's run at the release commit is recorded, every stage passed, the thread sanitizer's among them.

title: A C interface of create, push, pop, is-empty and destroy
body: The supplier shall provide a C11 header declaring an opaque ring type and the calls to create a ring of a given capacity, push a pointer, pop a pointer into the caller's variable, tell from the consumer whether the ring is empty, and destroy the ring setting the caller's pointer to NULL.
rationale: These are the five calls kyr_core's write queue makes; the type is held by pointer in each environment's queue.
criteria: The header compiles in a C11 consumer; the five calls exist with these shapes.

title: Statuses as return values
body: Creation shall return NULL when it fails; push and pop shall return 0 on success and -1 when the ring is full or empty (or not there), with no other effect on a refusal and no errno to read.
rationale: kyr_core tests the creation against NULL and every push and pop against 0.
criteria: Each refusal returns -1 and leaves the ring and the caller's variable as they were; a failed creation returns NULL.

title: Many pushing threads, one popping thread at a time
body: Push shall be safe from any number of threads at the same time, with no lock; pop and the emptiness check shall be made by one thread at a time, the writer's, then the stopping thread's after the writer is joined.
rationale: The request threads are the producers; the writer, and after its join the stopping thread, the consumer.
criteria: Under the thread sanitizer, many producers and one consumer run without a reported race.

title: The job popped is the job pushed, its contents visible
body: A pointer popped shall be exactly the one pushed, and what the submitter wrote into the job before its push shall be visible to the writer after its pop: the hand-off shall order the producer's writes before the consumer's reads (release on push, acquire on pop).
rationale: The writer runs the job's function on the job's context; a stale view of either is a wrong write.
criteria: An inspection of the memory ordering; the threaded suites deliver every value intact.

title: Linkage: versioned shared object and archive
body: The library shall be a shared object with a versioned soname and versioned symbols, exporting exactly its declared functions, and a static archive with the same functions.
rationale: kyr_core is linked statically into the box's servers, which load libmpscring at run time; a consumer built against another major must fail at load, not at run time.
criteria: The soname, the version node and the exports match the header.
